title: Python Syntax & Comments
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Python Syntax & Comments in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: What is syntax?
items.text: Syntax means the rules used to write valid Python code. If the rules are broken, Python can show a syntax-related error.

items.heading: Indentation
items.text: Indentation is the spaces at the beginning of a line. Python uses indentation to show which statements belong to a block.

items.heading: Code blocks
items.text: A block is a group of statements controlled by something such as if, for, while or a function. The statements in the block use consistent indentation.

items.heading: Colon after a header
items.text: A colon is normally placed after statements that start a block, such as if, for, while, def and class.

items.heading: Comments
items.text: A comment is a note for people reading the code. Python ignores a single-line comment that starts with #.

items.heading: Why comments help
items.text: Short, useful comments can explain why code exists or clarify a non-obvious step. Comments should not replace clear code.

items.heading: No normal braces for blocks
items.text: Python normally uses indentation instead of curly braces to mark blocks. This makes the visual structure part of the syntax.

items.heading: Consistent indentation
items.text: Using the same indentation style keeps code readable and prevents block-structure errors. Four spaces are the common style.

items.heading: IndentationError
items.text: Wrong or inconsistent indentation can raise IndentationError. Check the spaces before the affected statement.

items.heading: Readable structure
items.text: Good syntax is not only about avoiding errors; it also makes the program structure easy to follow.
